_comment: The Adventurer's Guild interior. FIXTURE-FIRST (near_guild -- the interior is the subject, not the street route): starts at (28,3) on the street, facing up at guild_door (28,2) -- issue #53 finding 13 moved the door into the facade line, so this fixture's start moved from (27,3)-facing-right in lockstep. Proves the door round-trip (street -> guild -> street, landing on sane open cells both ways), the desk+Selys interaction (pool-line absorb + her real graph, incl. the new desk-context node), the board and notice-wall dressed props, and walk-on pool lines (Renn, Ilvo, Yelra) -- the full DP1 surface. Seed 9 for convention; fixture rng_state governs (no combat in this script).

steps._comment: Bump guild_door (28,2) from (28,3) facing up -- the door is REAL now, no more toast. door moved from (28,3) to (28,2) (flush into the facade line); this fixture's start position/facing moved in lockstep from (27,3)-facing-right to (28,3)-facing-up.
steps.name: interact

steps._comment: Chronology: transition() fires map_changed synchronously, world.gd's handler rebuilds the field (mood/map/entities/lights/ambience) BEFORE control returns to wi_game.gd's interact() to record on_enter_accomplishment -- visited_guild is asserted AFTER the render events, matching the real event order.
blocked_cells 58 -> 57: the rug_woven_cream (8,4) crowded the only straight approach to Selys's desk -- unblocked, so the static list is one shorter.

Straight up the x=8 desk-gap column to Selys: up 7 to (8,3) (unblocked the (8,4) rug -- straight through it now, real positive proof the crowding is gone), then a blocked bump up against Selys herself (8,2) to set facing up (the SAME trailing-bump idiom door_awakening/etc. use).
SOCIAL S4 idiom: first talk to Selys this waking plays her rotating pool line; a second interact opens the real graph.

Fresh state: only 'Just looking around.' (idx0) and the new 'How does the board work?' (idx1) are visible -- has_package/lyonette_tip/package_delivered/errand_decided/chatted_with_selys:2 are all unmet.

payload_contains.speaker: Selys
payload_contains.text: The board's behind you. Reading it is free. Taking a posting means telling me, so I can log it and not have to chase you across Liscor. Anything else worth walking to, write it down — that's what the leads page in your journal is for.

steps._comment: West along y3 -- Renn (3,3) blocks the row, so the walk stops adjacent at (4,3) facing left.
Detour south around Renn/the board via the open y6 corridor, then the x1 column back up (Ilvo sits at (2,4) off this leg).
guild_notice_wall (2,5) blocks the step, so this bumps and interacts it from (2,6) facing up.

payload_contains.text: The smaller board, and nobody official keeps it: lost gear, rooms going spare, one duel challenge with nothing written under it. What is worth chasing copies into your journal as a lead, with a name and a place to start from.

steps._comment: guild_board (2,3) blocks the step from (1,3) facing right -- THE REQUEST BOARD went live in DP2: interact() now opens a code-built browse dialogue (header + the current active slate's copy from data/bounties.json + footer) instead of DP1's static toast. Full text/rotation-determinism assertions live in board_loop (DP2's own canonical); this script only proves the board stop on the DP1 walk still resolves cleanly through the new surface.
Only one option ('Step back from the board.') -- confirm at index 0 exits without moving the cursor.

steps._comment: Ilvo (2,4 -- diagonal from Renn so the duo reads as TWO Drakes, no y-sort occlusion) blocks the right leg at its FIRST step, from (1,4) facing right; the following left step bumps the x0 wall harmlessly and the Yelra approach is unchanged.

Yelra (12,6) blocks the step from (11,6) facing right.
